subject: observability and runbook health

the_declaration_driven_services_this_gat.gate32_observability_service: `resolve_observability` returns `production_monitoring: true` when a caller passes healthcheck_ready, support_owner_assigned, incident_escalation_ready and default_status='alert_ready'. Every input is a keyword argument. It measures nothing.
the_declaration_driven_services_this_gat.gate33_runbook_service: returns a hardcoded dict of six True values and a checklist whose evidence refs are `nf://` strings that point at nothing
the_declaration_driven_services_this_gat.why_not_extended: Gate 65 drew this line first and said so in its own module: those services model what a demo surface should display and will promote a status on any non-empty string. Gate 154 cannot produce a production_monitoring claim by any path.

what_is_observable_today: process liveness, from outside the app
the repository HEAD, the build stamp sha, the backend runtime mode
per-lane readiness, via each lane's own service
27 verifiers, each answering one question when run by hand
what_remains_manual: running verifiers, in an order the registry now records
noticing that a result is hours old; nothing records result age

what_was_not_observable_before_this_gate.backend_stale_code: the surface built to answer it does not. `/backend/health` calls `detect_git_identity` at REQUEST time, so it reports the repository's HEAD, not the commit the process loaded. Proved by editing a tracked file and watching `source_dirty` flip with no restart. Nothing records a process-scoped commit.
what_was_not_observable_before_this_gate.migration_drift: nothing compared the repository's highest revision to the database's current one. Gate 151 hit it at 0041 vs 0042 and found it by hand.
what_was_not_observable_before_this_gate.next_safe_action: a module constant in the Gate 144 summary, reading `finish_the_controlled_beta_readiness_matrix`. That was true at Gate 144; the matrix was finished at Gate 145 and nine gates have happened since. A constant cannot go stale loudly.
what_was_not_observable_before_this_gate.stale_build_stamp: `--strict-public` checks the stamp TAG exists. It never compares the stamped sha to HEAD, so a build from an older commit passes every check while serving old JavaScript.
what_was_not_observable_before_this_gate.verifier_dependency_order: no registry existed. An operator learned the order by running things and reading failures.
